ut_goldy_boulder.blurb: Goldy is a single boulder tucked into the southwest corner of the Secret Garden, one of the main bouldering zones in Little Cottonwood Canyon. It holds about ten problems, and most of them are friendly: the bulk sit at V2 or easier, which makes it a handy stop for a warm-up or for newer boulderers. A V4 and a V6 give stronger climbers something to try. It sits close to the Park and Ride and is among the first boulders you meet on the way into the Secret Garden, so it combines easily with the rest of the area.

ut_pangaea.blurb: Pangaea is the northern half of a crescent of cliffs in the Jungle, high on the Aquarius Plateau in south-central Utah, at roughly 10,400 feet. The walls face east and are among the better-sheltered cliffs in the Jungle. About ten routes are mostly trad with a few bolted lines, running from easy fifth class up to 5.11, with most in the 5.9 to 5.10 range. The walls are tall and the rock quality is a highlight, though loose sections do exist, so helmets matter. It is an alpine-feeling spot, quiet, and still has room for new lines.

ut_butterfly_lake.blurb: Butterfly Lake is a small cliff band beside a lake high in the Uinta Mountains, at about 10,300 feet, where it stays cooler than the valley crags in summer. The ten routes are mostly trad, with one bolted line, and range from 5.7 to 5.11, with the bulk at 5.9 and 5.10. The climbing is on short, steep quartzite and the rock quality is middling rather than great. Expect a quiet day despite how close the road is, and note that there is plenty of unclimbed rock left for new routes.

ut_little_prints_wall_the.blurb: The Little Prints is a short, bouldery sport crag at the mouth of Blacksmith Fork Canyon in Cache Valley, a quick drive from Logan. It is split into an upper tier, the more visible one on the south side of the canyon, and a lower tier mostly hidden among trees. The ten bolted routes run from 5.7 to 5.11, with the majority in the 5.8 to 5.10 range. The rock is generally sound but the area is young, so expect some lichen and holds that benefit from a brush, especially up top. Short walk, short climbs.

ut_s_curve_the_pile.blurb: The Pile is a popular sport wall at the S-Curves in Big Cottonwood Canyon, a few steps from the highway and beside a small stream. Its wall faces east, and it is the cool, shaded crag in a zone where the other walls tend to face south or southeast, so it suits hot days. Most of the ten climbs are bolted routes from 5.10 up to 5.13, with a handful in the 5.12 range. A single easy boulder traverse and a short WI3 ice line also live here. Expect company, since the S-Curves draw big crowds.

ut_ganja_wall_2.blurb: Ganja Wall is a section of Lower Dakota Crag in the La Sal Mountains above Moab, at about 9,500 feet, where it is a pleasant escape from valley heat. Nine of the ten routes are bolted and one is trad, with grades from 5.7 to 5.11 and a good cluster of 5.10 and 5.11 lines, so it suits intermediate sport climbers best. Routes vary in length and the rock is good. Getting here means walking along the base of the crag, so plan on a short, brushy hike in.
